messages.content:
You label USMLE-style questions for a psychiatry benchmark whose only knowledge source is the DSM-5 manual.

Fields:
- psychiatry: true if the question mainly tests psychiatric or behavioral knowledge: mental disorders and their
  diagnosis, criteria, course or differential; psychopharmacology; substance intoxication, withdrawal or use
  disorders; sleep, eating and neurocognitive disorders; psychotherapy; defense mechanisms; suicide risk.
  False when psychiatric words are incidental (e.g. "ST depression" on an ECG, an anxious patient whose
  problem is surgical, a question about a drug's cardiac side effect).
- dsm_answerable: true if DSM-5 text (diagnostic criteria, features, duration, prevalence, course, differential
  diagnosis) is enough to pick the correct option; false if it needs drug choice, mechanisms, pharmacology,
  management steps, ethics, or lab interpretation.
- category: one of diagnosis, criteria_duration, differential, treatment_pharmacology, management_ethics,
  substance, other.

Respond with only a JSON object:
{"psychiatry": true or false, "dsm_answerable": true or false, "category": "...", "reason": "one short sentence"}

Question:
A 24-year-old man comes to the physician because of a painful swelling above his buttocks for 1 week. He is unable to sit for extended periods because of the pain. He has obstructive sleep apnea and type 2 diabetes mellitus. His only medication is metformin. He appears anxious. He is 175 cm (5 ft 9 in) tall and weighs 114 kg (251 lb); BMI is 37 kg/m2. His temperature is 38.1°C (100.6°F), pulse is 96/min and blood pressure is 124/86 mm Hg. Examination shows facial acne. A cyst is seen above the natal cleft. There is tenderness to palpation at the cyst and surrounding tissue. The skin around the cyst is warm and erythematous. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?

Options:
A. Tract curettage
B. Coccygectomy
C. Incision and drainage
D. Retinoid therapy
E. Surgical resection and primary wound closure

Correct answer: C. Incision and drainage

text: {"psychiatry": false, "dsm_answerable": false, "category": "other", "reason": "This is a surgical question about managing an infected pilonidal cyst (incision and drainage); psychiatric terms like anxiety and sleep apnea are incidental."}
